correctness.rationale: Permuting leaves reduces each convex feasible region without objective loss to a two-parameter Gram matrix. Its exact Schur-complement eigenvalues imply q <= 2np(1-p)/(n-1), sharp by a regular-simplex Gram construction. Metric triangle inequalities add q<=2p and, for n>=3, q<=2/3. The resulting nondecreasing envelope proves every branch including all endpoints. In the cut polytope, a signed cut corresponds to a subset S with |S|=K, each membership mean <= epsilon, and leaf objective K(n-K). Concave interpolation plus a matching uniform random k/k+1 subset mixture gives its exact optimum. Expanding the interpolation proves the fractional-part defect. A standalone exact-rational test suite returned VERIFY_OK 7804 and independent finite linear programs LP_OK 95; these supplement rather than replace the full analytic proof.

originality.rationale: Full primary-source comparisons distinguish the claimed exact all-n star-conditioned support profile from exact spanning-tree integrality at zero tolerance, volume-based body comparisons, fixed-rank MaxCut approximation gaps, and deterministic cardinality-constraint approximation. A published-record index returned near neighbors but no statement covering the same constrained elliptope/triangle/cut comparison. The first five-vertex metric-versus-cut separation and the integer clique cut profile are explicitly prior, not independently novel. Residual risk includes older cut-polytope monographs and equivalent projected moment formulations.
residual_risks: Deza--Laurent and historical correlation-polytope literature were not exhaustively inspected at full book length; a preexisting symmetric star-marginal support formula or stronger lemma could imply the result.
Searching titles, abstracts, and indexed records cannot certify global novelty, and the published-record search cannot expose unpublished work.

The known metric/cut strict separation at five vertices and the elementary integer clique-cut profile are already known; originality is confined to their particular exact constrained SDP/cut phase comparison.

value.rationale: The motivating exact-spanning-tree integrality theorem creates a quantitative question: what can a near-decided star hide in the strengthened SDP? This natural complete-graph benchmark has a global all-size classification, a sharp phase switch at epsilon=1/n, the first positive gap at five total vertices, and an exact dimension-uniform additive gap at most 1/4. This is a structural constrained support-function benchmark, not a mere small finite calculation; no arbitrary-graph algorithmic improvement or false deterministic interpretation is claimed.
